questions.q: What does it mean to say rights and duties are "two sides of the same coin"?
questions.a: It means they are inseparable parts of a whole; you get a benefit (right) only when you accept a responsibility (duty). A wrong answer suggests the student thinks rights are free gifts or duties are punishments, missing the idea of balance.

questions.q: If you have the right to a clean park, what is your corresponding duty?
questions.a: Your duty is to not litter and to pick up your own trash. A wrong answer (like "telling the government to clean it") shows the student ignores their own individual role in maintaining the right.

questions.q: If your friend is exercising their right to speak, what duty do you have to ensure the balance of rights?
questions.a: Steps: 1. Identify the right (freedom of speech). 2. Identify the duty (active listening and respectful response). 3. Apply: I must listen without interrupting so they can finish their thought. 4. Verify: Does this allow both of us to communicate? A wrong answer shows an inability to link personal behavior to the rights of others.

questions.q: Why does a right to education come with a duty to study?
questions.a: Education requires resources provided by others; if you do not study, those resources are wasted, preventing others from having the same opportunity. A wrong answer suggests education is purely for personal gain rather than a social responsibility.

questions.q: Is it fair to claim a right without performing the duty that supports it? Why?
questions.a: No, because rights are maintained by the actions of all citizens; if everyone claimed rights but ignored duties, the community would fall apart. A wrong answer indicates a failure to understand social interdependence.

questions.q: Create a scenario where a duty is ignored and explain how a specific right is lost for others.
questions.a: If everyone ignores the duty to follow traffic rules (a duty for safety), the right to move freely on the roads safely disappears for everyone. A poor answer fails to connect the specific duty to the specific impact on the community.
